gloss: show signs of wanting to (of someone else)

definitions.gloss: to appear to want to; to be eager to
definitions.explanation: Verb stem plus たがる. Reports a desire that is visible from the outside, so it is used about a third person rather than about oneself: {弟|おとうと}は{行|い}きたがっている (my brother wants to go).

examples.english: The child wants to go outside.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{理由|りゆう}→理由：01102_riyuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{話|はな}したがらない→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: He doesn't want to talk about the reason.

examples.japanese: ⟦{妹|いもうと}→妹：00573_imouto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦ゲーム→ゲーム：03842_geemu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦やりたがっていて→やる：02980_yaru⟧、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My little sister is dying to play the new game and talks about nothing else every day.

notes:
Attaches to the verb stem and then conjugates like a godan verb: ⟦{行|い}き→行く：00119_iku⟧たがる, ⟦{行|い}きたがらない→行く：00119_iku⟧, ⟦{行|い}きたがった→行く：00119_iku⟧. The object of the wanted action takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧, not が.

USAGE:
- 〜たがって⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ describes what someone wants at this moment; plain 〜たがる describes a standing tendency.
- Do not use it about yourself — use 〜たい instead.
- About a superior or a customer it can sound presumptuous; 〜たい⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦おっしゃっています→おっしゃる：01299_ossharu⟧ is safer.

SIMILAR FORMS:
- 〜たい: want to — used for one's own desire, or in questions to the listener
- {欲|ほ}し⟦がる→〜がる：03089_garu⟧: to want (a thing) — the same third-person logic applied to objects rather than actions
